convoLines.text: "Let me be straight — Do you believe in anything? Now, I mean. After everything."
"That's not naive. That's load-bearing. Hold onto it."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
"Still on what you believe in. Just... be straight with me."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"I dreamed Consuelo was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
You show them Black Walnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Sleep's gone strange. I sharpen sticks down to nothing at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"What do you make of all this? Really."
"Bleak. Probably true. I keep looking for the part where it's not. Funny how that works."
"Still on what you make of all this."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
You walk to the hollow with Wei. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? Give it time."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Since Consuelo died... I keep expecting to see Consuelo at the fire. Stupid."
"I keep turning over the last thing Consuelo said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"This was good." They mean it.
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 4 days back. 'A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.'"
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on what's been happening."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"Heh. We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 4 days back. 'You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.'"
"Nobody says Consuelo's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
"I'm picking up Consuelo's share of the work. Someone should, and it might as well be me."
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Black Walnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Okay I really have to move now or I'll explode — talk soon!"
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good — what's been happening, settled. Feels better said out loud."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 7 days back. 'You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.'"
"My part? I sharpen sticks down to nothing and stay ready."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on what's been happening. That's still where we are."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"The pantry's nearly bare. Forage with me tomorrow? I know the creek bend, past the treeline."
"Another day like today and we're choosing who eats. Nobody's worked the creek bend, past the treeline in days. We'll fill packs before dark."

"Right. Action time. You know where to find me."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Black Walnut — I keep thinking about what you said. I'm seeing it everywhere now."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on that plant lesson."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Are you angry? At whoever did this. At the sky. At anything."
They nod. "Okay."
"Moving! But — good talk! More later!"
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
Violet: "You. Yeah, you. What do you make of this?"
"Take your time."
"This one — Camu-camu. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"Have you ever hurt someone? Since all this started."
They nod, slow. "Okay. Thank you for telling me. That couldn't have been easy to say."
"Still on whether you've hurt someone."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Good question." I've led people before. Real people, real stakes. Watch me work and tell me I'm wrong.
"Decisions don't make themselves. I learned that watching a group freeze once. Never again."
"I've got fires to light — metaphorical ones. Mostly."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"You called this the end of the world. We're still here, though. That's either something, or it's us."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on that personal stuff."
You show them Camu-camu — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."

"The stores won't stretch past tomorrow, and I'm not choosing who eats. I know the lotus patch past the treeline — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."

"Good question." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "The whole fire was arguing about The Static Kite last night — what to even CALL it. 'The Ugly Beast' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
"Gotta run. Literally. Bye!"
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"Can we talk?" Jason sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
Jason shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
They go very still. Not relaxed-still. Held-still.
"I wasn't a Pharmacist. I was a florist. The less of me is out there, the less can be used against me."
"You're really going to make me say it again?" Jason rubs their face. "Fine — but it's the same truth as last time."
"That again?" Jason sighs. "I confessed that already. I'm not confessing it twice for dramatic effect."
"We went over this," Jason says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."
"Do you still sing? ...Sorry — weird question. I just realized I haven't heard anyone sing. I'm sure it'll be fine."
"Ha! The creek concerts. I've heard those. Keep going."
"Still on whether you still sing."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
